description: The route planned on the phone scan of the real course (2026-11-06). Planned on 2026-11-07 by Kenny's route planner, used unchanged (drone_code/team_nav/team_nav/route_planner.py on origin/classical, commit 8d848da), on the map course_maps/phone_scan_2026-11-06.json with the mission missions/dronehacks_2026.json, cruise height 0.8 m. Converted to this file's frame with his start_frame.py: each waypoint is [forward, left] in metres from the launch mark, or [forward, left, height] where the leg into it must be flown at a height other than cruise (metres above the launch floor), with forward being where the nose points at takeoff, taken as 90 degrees from the course's east direction (north, along the first corridor), as in his route test and our simulator. The planner's first waypoint, the launch mark itself, is left out. Read by team_nav/mission_node.py when launched with mission:=route and route_file:=route_waypoints_scan.json.
planned_heights_note: The planner's height at each waypoint, for information. The route mission uses only the heights written as a third number in waypoints_forward_left_metres: 1.19 m at waypoints 22 and 23 (counting from 1), the planner's window crossing height (its 1.185 m, rounded to the centimetre). The window in this map is 0.81 to 1.56 m high. Every other leg is flown at cruise height.

planner_summary.numbering_note: Waypoint numbers here count from 1 in this file's list (the planner's numbers minus one). A leg numbered n runs from waypoint n to n+1, with leg 0 starting at the launch mark.
